newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices steady as gasoline signals conflict.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices steady as gasoline signals conflict.

text.p: Oil prices were stable on Wednesday as traders digested conflicting signals about the state of the gasoline market in the United States in the run-up to the peak summer driving season.

World benchmark North Sea Brent blend crude futures for June delivery shed nine cents to close at $18.52 a barrel after maintaining a slightly downward slant for most of the day, despite a brief rally towards the close prompted by technical buying. This compared with the contract's 34 cents rally on Tuesday.
Dealers said U.S. industry and government inventory data released this week failed to provide a seasonal lead for gasoline prices.
"Outright prices have been broadly ranging with other markets, reflecting gasoline's inability to truly dominate the complex thus far," said commodity brokers GNI Research in a report.

American Petroleum Institute (API) data showed U.S. gasoline stocks fell 408,000 barrels last week to 194.18 million barrels. Department of Energy figures recorded a modest 100,000 barrels rise last week.

And even though stocks are running far below last year's levels, dealers will need further convincing that a supply crunch this spring will push gasoline prices higher, dragging world crude markets in their wake.
"Inventories are almost nine million barrels below year ago, but we are not concerned by this until we see how peak demand is unfolding," said GNI.
The API estimates supply will be sufficient to accommodate demand growth of 2.5 percent and DOE data released on Wednesday showed 1997 gasoline demand running just 0.5 percent ahead.

"Stocks are extremely low and there's been no panic like there was in heating oil last fall," said Aaron Brady, analyst at Energy Security Analysis in Washington, citing soaring imports as the main reason for the market's relatively relaxed mood.

News that Tosco Corp would be restarting its 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) New Jersey Trainer refinery in the middle of next month, idle since February 1996, was also easing any worries about a shortfall in the northeast United States, traders said.

Higher refinery rates ahead of the peak gasoline season are helping to support crude prices, with cargoes of West African and North Sea oil flooding into the U.S. Gulf refining centre, but strong supply growth threatens to push prices lower again in the medium term unless gasoline demand accelerates, dealers said.
